goalBreakdown.reason: Contains apigenin, a compound that binds to brain receptors to promote relaxation and drowsiness.
Traditionally used to ease nervous tension. Studies show mild anxiolytic effects when consumed as tea.

warnings.message: You listed ragweed as an allergy. Chamomile is in the same plant family (Asteraceae) and may trigger a reaction.

uses.description: Widely used to promote relaxation and support restful sleep. Contains apigenin, which binds to brain receptors that reduce anxiety.
Soothes upset stomach, reduces bloating, and may relieve symptoms of IBS and indigestion.
Applied topically to calm irritated skin, reduce redness, and support wound healing.

contraindications.details: Chamomile is in the same family as ragweed. People with ragweed allergies may experience allergic reactions.
Chamomile contains coumarin, which may increase the effect of anticoagulant medications.
Large amounts may stimulate uterine contractions. Small amounts in tea are generally considered safe, but consult your doctor.

ingredients.name: Dried chamomile flowers
ingredients.notes: Use whole flowers for best flavor

steps.instruction: Place dried chamomile flowers into a tea infuser or directly into your cup.
steps.tip: A mesh ball infuser works great for loose flowers.

steps.instruction: Heat water to just below boiling (about 200°F / 93°C).
steps.tip: Boiling water can make the tea taste bitter.

steps.instruction: Pour hot water over the chamomile and let steep for 5-7 minutes.
steps.tip: Longer steeping = stronger flavor and more compounds extracted.

steps.instruction: Remove the infuser or strain the flowers. Add honey and lemon if desired.
Drink 30-60 minutes before bed for best sleep benefits.
steps.tip: Make it a nightly ritual to signal your body it's time to wind down.

steps.instruction: Fill your glass jar about halfway with dried chamomile flowers.
steps.tip: Don't pack too tightly — the alcohol needs to circulate.

steps.instruction: Pour vodka over the flowers until they are fully submerged with about 1 inch of liquid above.
Seal the jar tightly and label it with the date.
Store in a cool, dark place for 4-6 weeks. Shake the jar gently every few days.
steps.tip: A kitchen cabinet away from the stove works perfectly.

steps.instruction: After 4-6 weeks, strain through cheesecloth into a dark dropper bottle.
steps.tip: Squeeze the cheesecloth to get every last drop.

steps.instruction: Take 1-2 dropperfuls (30-60 drops) in water or tea as needed.
steps.tip: Start with a smaller dose to see how your body responds.
